source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes
recommendations: Initiate lifestyle modification including medical nutrition therapy
Weight reduction of 5-7% of body weight if overweight or obese
At least 150 minutes per week of moderate-intensity aerobic activity
Metformin as first-line pharmacotherapy if not contraindicated
Consider SGLT2 inhibitor or GLP-1 RA if established cardiovascular or renal disease
Comprehensive diabetes self-management education and support (DSMES)

follow_up.action: Initiate lifestyle changes and diabetes education
Repeat HbA1c to assess glycemic response
Reassess treatment plan; intensify therapy if HbA1c not at goal
Comprehensive metabolic panel, lipid profile, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio

contraindications.action: Dose reduction required; do not initiate new therapy
Avoid due to increased hypoglycemia risk
Not recommended for glycemic control below this threshold

emergency_signs: Diabetic ketoacidosis: nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, fruity breath, Kussmaul breathing
Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state: extreme hyperglycemia (>600 mg/dL), altered consciousness
Severe hypoglycemia: confusion, seizures, loss of consciousness
references: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes — 2025. Diabetes Care 2025;48(Suppl. 1)

source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes
recommendations: Prediabetes — initiate intensive lifestyle intervention program
Target weight loss of at least 7% of body weight
Physical activity: 150+ minutes per week of moderate-intensity exercise
Consider metformin for prediabetes prevention in high-risk individuals (BMI ≥ 35, age < 60, history of gestational diabetes)

follow_up.action: Reassess weight, HbA1c, and fasting glucose
Repeat HbA1c and fasting glucose to monitor for progression to diabetes

references: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes — 2025. Diabetes Care 2025;48(Suppl. 1)

source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes
section: Section 10 — Cardiovascular Disease and Risk Management
recommendations: Statin therapy: high-intensity for patients with established ASCVD
Blood pressure target < 130/80 mmHg if tolerated
ACE inhibitor or ARB for patients with albuminuria
SGLT2 inhibitor with proven cardiovascular benefit (empagliflozin, canagliflozin, dapagliflozin)
GLP-1 receptor agonist with proven cardiovascular benefit (liraglutide, semaglutide, dulaglutide)
Aspirin 75-162 mg/day for secondary prevention in patients with established ASCVD

follow_up.action: Initiate or optimize statin and blood pressure therapy
Comprehensive cardiovascular risk assessment and lipid panel

emergency_signs: Acute coronary syndrome: chest pain, shortness of breath, diaphoresis
Stroke symptoms: sudden weakness, speech difficulty, facial droop
Acute kidney injury: oliguria, edema, rapid creatinine rise
references: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes — 2025. Diabetes Care 2025;48(Suppl. 1)
